title: They All Played Ragtime: Tony Parenti, old friends and the 1914 ragtime contest
summary: Allen shows a ragtime book naming Tony Parenti and others. Leclerc notes who is still alive, and does not recall the 1914 ragtime contest or Kid Ross.

story.theme_name: Illness, injury and the deaths of colleagues
story.community_name: Illness, injury and death among jazz musicians

blocks.x: Did you ever see this book called They All Played Ragtime? No, I did not. Well, let's look at this third paragraph here. Tony Perrini, the New Orleans clarinet player.
Tony's still living, I think. He's in Chicago. No, he's in New York.
Last time I talked to him... Oh, that's right.
He started his own club there now. Oh, he did? Yeah, he's back on 52nd Street. They're opening up 52nd Street.

Yeah, I'm happy to hear that. Tony was wonderful. He was named several property units. Oh, I bought Tom Zimmerman. Oh, poor Tom. I'm still here. And Eddie McCarty's gone. Karma Comic is gone. Yeah, isn't that something?
Yeah, Roy Barton. Yeah, I remember that. And told Tom. Henry Regis, too. Yeah. Isn't that something?
Do you remember that contest? It's all in print, boy. Do you remember that ragtime contest? No, honestly, I don't. For Kid Ross? Do you remember Kid Ross?
I remember the name, yes. Yeah, well, Kid Ross, my brother's sporting... Yeah, that's right. Tango belt.
Yeah. Yeah. Roy remember the ragtime contest. Oh, yeah, for White Sonley. Isn't that funny? 1914, Leclerc and Kid Ross among the entrants. Isn't that something?
And you don't remember any ragtime?
Did you win any medals, ever? No. Loving Cubs? Nothing like that. No.
Maybe they didn't get them out in those days.
